Early oral intake is not necessarily limited solely to laparoscopic surgery. While it is true that some patients may require a longer period of postoperative oral intake after laparotomy and colorectal resection, this does not mean that early oral intake should be limited.

The American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE) recommends that patients who undergo gastrointestinal surgery should have adequate oral intake as soon as possible after surgery to prevent complications such as aspiration pneumonia. However, the extent of early oral intake will depend on individual patient factors, including their overall health, surgical complexity, and any underlying medical conditions.

It's essential to note that early oral intake is not a contraindication to laparoscopic surgery, but rather an important aspect of postoperative care. Patients should work closely with their healthcare provider to determine the best approach for their specific needs and circumstances.

In summary, while some patients may require a longer period of postoperative oral intake after laparoscopy, it is not necessarily limited solely to this type of surgery. A more nuanced approach that takes into account individual patient factors and surgical complexity is recommended.
